description: The skill's sections as one page

children.name: Headline
children.content: Plan next week's rota in ten minutes.

children.name: What it is, and for whom
children.content: Harbour Rota is shift planning for ferry and harbour crews. It knows who is rested, licensed and willing, and shows you which shifts still need someone.

children.name: Reassurance
children.content: No card needed. 240 crews planned this week with it.
Rested, has the ferry desk licence, asked for more hours
Works the night before: rest time too short

children.name: Heading
children.content: An open shift comes with the people who can take it.

children.name: Text
children.content: Rest time, licences and contract hours are checked before a name is offered. You choose; the rota never puts someone on a shift they may not work.
to fill a week by phone
with Harbour Rota, at Sotra Havn
Hours that stay inside the contract
Every change shows what it does to each person's week, before you publish.
Two people agree in the app. You get one question: yes or no.
Aksel and Ingrid want to swap Saturday. Both stay under 37.5 hours.

children.name: Quote
children.content: “I used to spend Sunday evening on the phone. Now the rota is out on Thursday and nobody calls me about it.”
to plan a week, down from 38

children.name: Heading
children.content: A price per harbour, not per head.
For one desk and up to eight people.
Billed yearly as NOK 4,900. Any number of people.
Rest time, licences and contract hours checked
Open shifts offered to those who can take them
Billed yearly as NOK 14,900. Several harbours.
Something else? Write to hei@harbour-rota.example and a person in Bergen answers.
Do my crew need to install anything?
No. They get the rota as a link that opens on any phone. The app is there for those who want to swap shifts or be told about open ones.
